title: Orchid Health — outreach & pilot play notes
content:
Context:
- Account: Orchid Health (regional telemedicine chain; 18 clinics, primary care + urgent telemed).
- Why target: high doc burden, growing telehealth volumes, explicit pitch for clinician time savings and coding accuracy. They mentioned interest in automation at HL7/FHIR layer in last webinar.

High-level positioning for outreach:
- Redwood as an inference platform partner (not just an API): focus on predictable latency for live consult summarization, PHI-safe deployment options (private VPC or on-prem), and measurable cost/per-visit economics.
- Pilot goal: shave 1.5–3 minutes off clinician note time per consult; surface structured problem list / billing codes and quick patient summary for follow-up.

Key contacts & intel (notes from LinkedIn + last demo):
- Dr. Aisha Rahman — Chief Medical Officer (clinical champion). Prefers clinical evidence, case studies.
- Omar Velasquez — VP of Engineering (integration lead). Responsible for EHR integrations, mentions Epic + athena in tech stack.
- Jenna Park — Director of Compliance. Very sensitive to data flow and KMS / logging.
- Sales/Procurement: TBD (procurement typically 8–12 weeks).
- Recent notes: They piloted a transcription vendor (X) and got pushback on accuracy and PHI contract terms. Interested in private deployment if SLAs + audit logs OK.

Top pain points to call out:
- Accuracy & hallucination risk (regulatory exposure).
- PHI management & auditability (KMS, HSM, retention policies).
- Integration friction with Epic/athena (FHIR/HL7 mapping).
- Per-consult unit economics and predictable latency (real-time and post-visit batch).

Messaging hooks (short):
- "Secure, low-latency summarization that fits inside your EHR workflow — on VPC or on-prem, auditable keys, can run within your network."
- "Pilot to show 20–35% reduction in note time for PCPs with configurable safety filters and rollback policy."
- "We route requests to a private model variant that gives you deterministic perf at scale — we can set SLOs for median latency and error fallbacks."

Pilot scope (recommended simple starter):
- Duration: 6 weeks + 2-week ramp.
- Population: 8–12 clinicians (mix of PCP + urgent care).
- Use-cases: visit summarization (structured summary + problem list), suggested billing codes (CPT), quick patient action-items.
- Integration: batched HL7->FHIR payloads into a sandbox Epic instance; Azure/AWS VPC peering for Private deployment or on-prem box if they request.
- Success metrics: 
  - Avg reduction in documentation time per consult (target >= 1.5 minutes).
  - Precision of suggested codes (target >= 85% on a small eval set).
  - Clinician satisfaction NPS delta (pre/post).
- Security checklist: PHI not persisted outside customer VPC; KMS integration; audit logs per request; optional HSM for keys.

Objections & suggested responses (shorthand):
- "We can't risk PHI in a 3rd-party cloud." -> "We support Private with customer-managed VPC and can provide an on-prem option; full audit logs and KMS/HSM integration. We'll draft a SOC2/HIPAA addendum and a narrow data flow diagram for legal."
- "How do you handle hallucinations?" -> "Layered approach: model selection + prompt safety guards + post-filter rules + clinician-in-the-loop. We'll set a conservative model/temperature for clinical pilot and surface confidence scores and provenance for each claim."
- "Epic integration is painful." -> "We partner at the HL7/FHIR boundary, can do an initial sandbox integration via SFTP or secure API to accelerate. Engineering (Omar) usually wants a small POC mapping first — propose dedicated SRE touch for integration week."
- "What's the cost?" -> "Pilot pricing: fixed pilot fee covering infra + onboarding. Post-pilot, two options: usage-based hosted with predictable per-token budgets or Dedicated reserved capacity for consistent throughput and lower unit cost. Show numbers once we scope volume."

Email draft (first reach — concise):
Subject: quick pilot idea to reduce clinician note time at Orchid Health
Hi Aisha / Omar —
I liked your recent webinar on telemedicine workflows. Short idea: Redwood can run a 6-week pilot to deliver structured visit summaries + suggested CPT codes inside a sandbox Epic instance (private VPC or on-prem), with measurable clinician time savings and auditable PHI handling.
Curious if you'd be open to a 20–30 minute call next week to sketch a minimal pilot (no long legal strings up-front)? Happy to include Priya from product and Marcus from integrations.
Thanks — Lena

LinkedIn touch (short):
Hi Aisha — enjoyed your talk at TeleHealth Summit. I help run pilots for inference-driven clinical summaries at Redwood — would love to share a short pilot outline if you're open.

Voicemail script:
"Hi Aisha, Lena Park at Redwood. Quick note — we ran a 6-week pilot at a CHC that cut clinician note time by ~2 minutes per visit. I'd love 15 minutes to see if a similar approach could help Orchid. I'll follow up via email. Thanks!"

Meeting prep checklist (if call booked):
- Bring 2–page pilot one-pager + security/dataflow diagram.
- Ask: current per-visit doc time, EHR vendor details (versions), expected consult volume per clinician, compliance signoff path.
- Demo plan: 8-minute walkthrough of clinician summarization UX; show fallbacks + logs.
- Attendees to include: Marcus (integrations), Priya (product), me.

Action items / TODO (personal):
- [ ] Draft pilot one-pager (deadline 11/05) — include pricing bands.
- [ ] Get SOC2/HIPAA scoping doc from security (ask security@redwood).
- [ ] Create sample FHIR mapping example (Epic -> summary fields) — Marcus to produce.
- [ ] Mock evaluation dataset: anonymized 50 visits for initial accuracy checks. Try to request from Orchid during intro.
- [ ] Prep sandbox deployment plan (VPC peering steps).

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Jenna (compliance) likely to request data retention and deletion SLA. Need standard language and timeline for deletion.
- Check whether Orchid has a BRB (Business Associate Agreement) template. If not, legal will need 2–3 weeks.
- Consider offering an initial in-person workshop for clinical champions to increase buy-in.

Quick competitive intelligence:
- Vendor X (transcription) failed mainly on domain-specific terminology and slow turnaround.
- Vendor Y offers hosted-only solution — good for speed but not for customers requiring private deployments. Use this to push Redwood's unified hosted/dedicated/private angle.

Small script for discovery on first call:
1) "Walk me through a typical televisit and the top three bottlenecks for your clinicians."
2) "If we shaved X minutes per visit, what would success look like operationally?"
3) "Who would need to sign off for a security-limited pilot (legal/compliance/procurement timeline)?"

End of notes.

(Keep this as personal scratchpad — will convert to one-pager after first call.)
